chapter_name: Exploration: Entering the World of Secondary Science
learning_objective: 🎯 Think like a scientist! Master the scientific method, learn how to conduct fair experiments, and understand essential laboratory safety rules.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: चर (Something that changes in an experiment)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Science isn't just facts; it's a process! It involves asking a question, doing background research, forming a hypothesis, conducting an experiment, analyzing data, and drawing a conclusion.

An observation is a fact you gather using your five senses (e.g., 'The liquid turned blue'). An inference is a logical conclusion you make based on that observation (e.g., 'A chemical reaction occurred').
In a fair test, you only change ONE thing at a time. The Independent Variable is what YOU change. The Dependent Variable is what you MEASURE. Controlled variables are what you keep the SAME.

Science relies on the International System of Units (SI). We use meters for length, kilograms for mass, and seconds for time. Accuracy is how close you are to the true value; precision is how consistent your measurements are.
The lab is a place for discovery, not danger! Always wear safety goggles, tie back long hair, never taste chemicals, and know where the emergency equipment (like the eye wash station) is located.

fun_activity.title: 🍏 The Gravity Drop Experiment
fun_activity.instructions: Hold a heavy book and a crumpled piece of paper at the same height. Drop them at the exact same time. Do they hit the ground together? You just performed an observation to test a hypothesis about gravity!

exam_tips: 📌 Always be able to identify the Independent and Dependent variables in a given experiment scenario. This is a classic test question.
📌 Know the standard SI units for basic measurements (e.g., Temperature is Kelvin, not Celsius).
📌 When reading a liquid's volume in a graduated cylinder, always read from the bottom of the curve (the meniscus) at eye level.
quick_recap: ⭐ A hypothesis must be testable to be scientifically valid.
⭐ Changing more than one variable at a time ruins an experiment because you won't know which change caused the result.
⭐ Safety first: Treat every chemical in the lab as if it were hazardous.
